q-42570.name: Question 1
q-42570.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 2 & -4 \\ -1 & -4 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{21}$ equal to zero.*
q-42570.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -5 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 2 & -4 \\ -1 & -4 & -8 & 8\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -5 & 4 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & -8 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -5 & 4 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & -8 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -8 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -6 & -8 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-42919.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -6 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -1 & 10 & 1\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{13}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*

Using elementary row operations, let's make entries below ${a}_{13}=-2$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -6 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & -1 & 10 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 & -7 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -11 & 0 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 & -7 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -11 & 0 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}0 & 10 & -7 \\ -1 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -11 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 10 & -7 \\ -1 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -11 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}10 & -7 \\ -11 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(110-77) \\  & =-66.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=3$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}9 & 3 & 6 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-3){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-2){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 5 & 3 \\ 8 & -2 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 5 & 3 \\ 8 & -2 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 3 \\ 8 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 & 3 \\ 8 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-132144.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
q-132144.worked_solution:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries above and below ${a}_{32}=3$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-1){R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot -3\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =9(30+6) \\  & =324.\end{aligned}
$$
